item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL operated under a statutory framework congruent with the 2019–2024 National Development Plan and Social Welfare Sector Program. Its stated functions included coordinating social-policy evaluation, defining and measuring poverty, and generating analyses and recommendations intended for decision-makers. The excerpt does not establish López Obrador’s personal direction or use of the evidence.","notes":["The excerpt supports the planning-framework alignment and CONEVAL’s functions and stated objective.","“Formal mandate” to issue evidence-based recommendations is narrowed because the mandate explicitly cited concerns evaluation and poverty measurement, while recommendations appear as an institutional objective/output."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["All reported figures and comparisons are stated in the excerpt.","The summary appropriately avoids attributing causal responsibility to López Obrador."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 80.4% improvement figure, 7,136 high- or very-high-lag localities, and 5,258 persistent-lag localities.","It also supports the stated municipal coverage and below-one beneficiary-to-poverty ratios for the older-person pension, disability pension, and Sembrando Vida."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The updated Social Rights Information System contained 179 indicators, including measures of effective access and inequality for women Indigenous people, youth, older people, people with disabilities, and gender gaps. From 2018 to 2022, the share of people aged 65 or older receiving a pension at least equal to the national income-poverty line rose from 26.0% to 35.2%, while the share of employed Indigenous women at or above that line was 33.8%, compared with 62.8% for non-Indigenous women.","notes":["The excerpt supports 179 indicators, the listed population groups, the 26.0%–35.2% change, and the 33.8% versus 62.8% comparison.","The wording is narrowed to the excerpt’s population definitions and avoids implying that the figures are causal policy effects."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 263-indicator classifications of 47% important progress and 53% insufficient, lagging, or very lagging.","It also supports the 141 pandemic-affected indicators classified as 27% surpassed and 47% very lagging."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 16.2% nominal increase for social-program budgets, the 28.1% nominal increase for 15 priority programs, and the 512,806-million-peso budget for 16 priority programs.","It supports the 69%, 50%, and 38% program-quality figures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported strong execution of its own evaluation and monitoring program in 2023: 95% of registered improvement commitments were completed, 95% of evaluations were disseminated, 173 mandated evaluations met CONEVAL criteria, and use of CONEVAL information increased by 34% over the 2012–2022 average. At the same time, indicators were approved for only 45 of 58 social programs.","notes":["The excerpt reports rounded values of 95%, 95%, and 34%, not 94.9%, 95.3%, and 34.4%.","The remaining figures and attribution to institutional performance are supported."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported that the ASF’s 2023 audit no. 90 found no observations, the internal audit of program P003 received a clean opinion, and the personnel-contracting audit found no definitive findings. The institution also reported completion of all 21 internal-control improvement actions and 100% completion of risk-mitigation actions.","notes":["The excerpt supports these specific audit and control results.","The broader claim that all external and internal oversight actions were completed without unresolved findings is narrowed because the excerpt covers multiple actions with differing statuses and does not support that universal formulation."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0054-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported institutional ethics and transparency measures in 2023, including approval and publication of a code of conduct, zero-tolerance statements on corruption and sexual harassment, ethics-committee renewal, conflict-of-interest training or dissemination activities, 149 of 155 information requests attended during the year, and compliance with transparency-portal updates; one of three review appeals revoked a CONEVAL response.","notes":["The excerpt supports approval and publication of the code, rather than specifically describing it as revised.","The excerpt supports conflict-of-interest-related dissemination activities, but not a quantified training completion claim.","The transparency figures and appeal outcome are supported."]}]}
